title: Cross-environment priority fallback hotfix for token surge causing TTFT and throughput collapse
creator: Marco Chen
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported sudden TTFT regressions and ~3-6x drop in tokens/sec for mixed workload models after runtime 2.4.0 rollout. Symptom set: large variance in first-token latency, long-tail TPS collapse during short bursts, and sustained KV cache miss amplification for sessions with heterogeneous sequence lengths. Initial traces point at our new preemptive kernel scheduling and an aggressive continuous-batching heuristic that together cause small requests to wait behind large context batches and trigger worker-level GC spikes. This ticket is the umbrella for immediate mitigations, short-term rollback plans, and a targeted RCA. Goals: 1) restore acceptable TTFT for impacted customers within the SLA window; 2) deploy a safe fallback that preserves throughput for long-running sessions; 3) produce a definitive RCA and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Marco Chen: Customer A (enterprise VPC) and Customer B (hosted PLG) began reporting elevated first-token latencies ~09:00 UTC. Pager triggered. Gathered traces and initial histograms in Grafana.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Aisha Patel: Correlated incidents to runtime-2.4.0 kernel preemption flag (flag:kernel_preempt=true) and the continuous-batching window change (config:batch_window_ms=20->50). Short sequences now starve behind long-context microbatches.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Dev Ops: Deployed emergency router rule to prioritize requests with sequence_length <= 64 for high-tier customers. Immediate TTFT improvement for 2/3 impacted customers; still failing for one Dedicated customer with heavy multi-model fanout.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Sofia Alvarez (Eng Reviewer): Suggested toggling kernel_preempt=false on a subset of workers as a controlled rollback. Noted trade-off: slightly higher long-tail CPU occupancy but reduces preemption stalls causing KV cache churn.

2026-03-10 15:30 - Aisha Patel: Rolled kernel_preempt=false to 10% canary in us-west; observed tokens/sec recover ~2.5x on canary within 15 minutes. Opened PR to add safe config flag and rollout script.
2026-03-11 08:12 - Customer Success: Customer C (Dedicated) escalated due to SLA violations overnight. Coordinating for dedicated patch release and on-prem instructions for Private customers.

2026-03-11 12:50 - Marco Chen: Deployed priority-fallback router change: short requests + high-priority customers bypass batching window. Measured TTFT P50 drop from 420ms -> 95ms for short requests; overall tokens/sec still 20% under baseline for mixed sessions.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Aisha Patel: Work in progress on deterministic batch sizing logic (avoid indefinite wait behind long contexts) and a KV cache stabilizer to reduce churn. Planning staged rollout next 48 hours. Added follow-up tickets for thorough regression tests and perfbench.
2026-03-12 11:30 - Product: Notified impacted customers of mitigation steps and ETA for broader fix. Providing runbook for Dedicated/Private to apply kernel_preempt=false patch.

2026-03-12 12:05 - QA: Creating synthetic mixtest harness scenarios covering short spike bursts and heterogeneous sequence distributions to validate both performance and correctness under fallback configs.
next_steps: Finish canary rollout of kernel_preempt=false to all worker pools in Hosted and Dedicated (Ops)
Publish step-by-step patch for Private customers and coordinate with Solutions Eng for on-prem installs
Ship deterministic batching logic (server-side heuristic) to avoid starvation of short requests
Stabilize KV cache eviction thresholds under mixed workloads and add metrics to detect churn early
Complete postmortem and schedule a post-deploy perf hunt to validate tokens/sec baseline across model families
